readings.title: A Command Against Normal Life
readings.subtitle: No Marriage, No Family, No Mourning
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 16:1] And <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] <dq>“Do not take <dn>את</dn> a wife, nor have sons or daughters in this place.”</dq>
[3] <dq>For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sons and daughters who are born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bear them and their fathers who bring them forth in this land,</dq>
[4] <dq>“They shall die of deaths from diseases, they shall not be lamented nor be buried, but be like dung on <dn>את</dn> the face of the earth, and be consumed by sword and by scarcity of food. And their corpses shall be meat for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.”</dq>

readings.title: The Withdrawal of Peace
readings.subtitle: Exile for Stubborn Disobedience
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 16:5] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Do not enter the house of mourning, neither go to lament or mourn for them, for <dn>I</dn> have withdrawn <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> peace from this people,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“even <dn>את</dn> the loving-commitment and <dn>את</dn> the compassions.</dq>
[6] <dq>“Both great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, and no one shall lament for them, or cut themselves, or make themselves bald for them.</dq>
[7] <dq>“Neither shall they break bread in mourning for them to comfort them for the dead, nor give them <dn>את</dn> the cup of comfort to drink for their father or their mother.</dq>
[8] <dq>“Do not enter the house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.”</dq>
[9] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“See, before your eyes and in your days, <dn>I</dn> am making <dn>את</dn> the voice of rejoicing and <dn>את</dn> the voice of gladness, <dn>את</dn> the voice of the bridegroom and <dn>את</dn> the voice of the bride to cease in this place.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And it shall be, when you declare to this people <dn>את</dn> all these words, and they shall say to you, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pronounced all this great evil against us? And what is <dn>את</dn> our crookedness, and what is <dn>את</dn> our sin that we have committed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>?’</dq>
[11] <dq>then you shall say to them, ‘Because your fathers have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and have walked after other mighty ones and served them and bowed themselves to them, and have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>, and did not guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Torah.</dq>
[12] <dq>And you have done more evil than your fathers, for look, each one walks according to the stubbornness of his own evil heart, without listening to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[13] <dq>So <dn>I</dn> shall throw <dn>את</dn> you out of this land into a land that you do not know, neither you nor your fathers. And there you shall serve other mighty ones day and night, where <dn>I</dn> show you no favour.’</dq>

readings.title: A New Exodus and a Present Reckoning
readings.subtitle: Hunters, Fishermen, and Double Repayment for Sin
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 16:14] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when it is no longer said, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives who brought up <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl from the land of Mitsrayim,’</dq>
[15] <dq>but, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives who brought up <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl from the land of the north and from all the lands where <dn>He</dn> had driven them.’ For <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back into their land <dn>I</dn> gave to their fathers.</dq>
[16] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am sending for many fishermen,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and they shall fish them. And after that <dn>I</dn> shall send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain and every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks.</dq>
[17] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> eyes are on all their ways; they have not been hidden from <dn>My</dn> face, nor has their crookedness been hidden from <dn>My</dn> eyes.</dq>
[18] <dq>“And first <dn>I</dn> shall repay double for <dn>את</dn> their crookedness and <dn>את</dn> their sin, because they have defiled <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> land with the dead bodies of their disgusting matters, and have filled <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> inheritance with their abominations.”</dq>

readings.title: The Nations Will Seek YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: “They Shall Know That My Name is YeHoVaH”
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 16:19] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my strength and my stronghold and my refuge, in the day of distress the nations shall come to You from the ends of the earth and say, “Our fathers have inherited only falsehood, futility, and there is no value in them.”
[20] Would a man make mighty ones for himself, which are not mighty ones?
[21] <dq>“Therefore see, <dn>I</dn> am causing them to know, this time <dn>I</dn> cause them to know <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> might. And they shall know that <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!”</dq>

readings.title: Sin Engraved on the Heart
readings.subtitle: The Forfeiture of Inheritance
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 17:1] <dq>“The sin of Yehuḏah is written with a pen of iron, engraved with the point of a diamond on <dn>את</dn> the tablet of their heart, and on the horns of your slaughter-places,</dq>
[2] <dq>while their children remember <dn>את</dn> their slaughter-places and <dn>את</dn> their Ashěrim by the spreading trees on the high hills.</dq>
[3] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> mountain in the field, <dn>I</dn> give as plunder <dn>את</dn> your wealth, all your treasures, your high places of sin, throughout all your borders.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And you, even of yourself, shall let go of <dn>את</dn> your inheritance which <dn>I</dn> gave you. And <dn>I</dn> shall make you serve <dn>את</dn> your enemies in a land which you have not known, for you have kindled a fire in <dn>My</dn> displeasure which burns forever.”</dq>

readings.title: The Two Ways
readings.subtitle: Cursed is the Man Who Trusts in Man, Blessed is the Man Who Trusts in YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 17:5] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart turns away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[6] <dq>“For he shall be like a shrub in the desert, and not see when good comes, and shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land that is not inhabited.</dq>
[7] <dq>“Blessed is the man who trusts in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and whose trust is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[8] <dq>“For he shall be like a tree planted by the waters, which spreads out its roots by the river, and does not see when heat comes. And his leaf shall be green, and in the year of drought he is not anxious, nor does he cease from yielding fruit.</dq>
[9] <dq>“The heart is crooked above all, and desperately sick – who shall know it?</dq>
[10] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, search <dn>את</dn> the heart, <dn>I</dn> try <dn>את</dn> the kidneys, and give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.</dq>

readings.title: The Fountain of Living Waters
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah's Plea for Healing and Vindication
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 17:11] “As a partridge that broods but does not hatch, so is he who gets riches, but not by right. It leaves him in the midst of his days, and at his end he is a fool.”
[12] An esteemed throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our set-apart place.
[13] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the expectation of Yisra’ěl, all who forsake You are put to shame. “Those who depart from Me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>את</dn> the fountain of living waters.”
[14] Heal me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that I am healed. Save me, so that I am saved, for You are my praise.
[15] See, they say to me, “Where is the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Let it come now!”
[16] And I have not run away from being a shepherd who follows You, nor have I longed for the desperately sick day. You Yourself have known, that which came out of my lips was before You.
[17] Do not be a ruin to me, You are my shelter in the day of evil.
[18] Let these who persecute me be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be broken, but do not let me be broken. Bring on them the day of evil, and destroy them with double destruction!

readings.title: A Message at the City Gates
readings.subtitle: The Sabbath as a Test of Obedience
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 17:19] Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, by which the sovereigns of Yehuḏah come in and by which they go out, and in all the gates of Yerushalayim.</dq>
[20] <dq>“And you shall say to them, ‘Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you sovereigns of Yehuḏah, and all Yehuḏah, and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, who enter by these gates.</dq>
[21] <dq>Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Guard <dn>את</dn> yourselves, and bear no <dn>את</dn> burden on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Yerushalayim,</dq>
[22] <dq>nor take <dn>את</dn> a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath day, nor do any work. And you shall set apart <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day, as <dn>I</dn> commanded your fathers.</dq>
[23] <dq>“But they did not obey, or incline their ear, and they made their neck stiff not to hear and not to receive instruction.</dq>
[24] <dq>“And it shall be, if you diligently obey <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and set apart <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day, to do no work in it,</dq>
[25] <dq>then sovereigns and heads sitting on the throne of Daviḏ shall enter in through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their heads – the men of Yehuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim. And this city shall be inhabited forever.</dq>
[26] <dq>“And they shall come from the cities of Yehuḏah and from the places around Yerushalayim, and from the land of Binyamin and from the low country, from the mountains and from the South, bringing ascending offerings and slaughterings, grain offerings and incense, bringing offerings of praise to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[27] <dq>“But if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn> to set apart <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day, and not to bear a burden when entering the gates of Yerushalayim on the Sabbath day, then <dn>I</dn> shall kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall consume <dn>את</dn> the palaces of Yerushalayim, and not be quenched.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Potter and the Clay
readings.subtitle: A Nation's Destiny is in YeHoVaH's Hand
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 18:1] The word which came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[2] <dq>“Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there <dn>I</dn> let you hear <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words.”</dq>
[3] So I went down to the potter’s house, and saw him doing a piece of work on the wheel.
[4] And <dn>את</dn> the vessel that he made of clay was ruined in the hand of the potter, so he remade it into another vessel, as it seemed good to the potter to do.
[5] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[6] <dq>“O house of Yisra’ěl, am <dn>I</dn> not able to do with you as this potter?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Look, as the clay is in the hand of the potter, so are you in <dn>My</dn> hand, O house of Yisra’ěl!</dq>
[7] <dq>“The moment <dn>I</dn> speak concerning a nation and concerning a reign, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it,</dq>
[8] <dq>and that nation shall turn from its evil because <dn>I</dn> have spoken against it, then <dn>I</dn> shall repent of <dn>את</dn> the evil that <dn>I</dn> thought to do to it.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And the moment <dn>I</dn> speak concerning a nation and concerning a reign, to build and to plant it,</dq>
[10] <dq>and it shall do evil in <dn>My</dn> eyes in not obeying <dn>My</dn> voice, then <dn>I</dn> shall repent concerning <dn>את</dn> the good with which <dn>I</dn> spoke of doing to it.</dq>
[11] <dq>“And now, speak to <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>I</dn> am forming evil and devising a plan against you. Return now every one from his evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.” ’ ”</dq>
[12] But they shall say, “It is no use! For we walk according to our own plans, and we do each one the stubbornness of his evil heart.”
[13] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Ask now among the nations, who has heard the like of this? The maiden of Yisra’ěl has done what is most horrible.</dq>
[14] <dq>“Does the snow of Leḇanon cease from the rock of the field? Or the cool flowing waters from afar dry up?</dq>
[15] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> people have forgotten <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>, they have burned incense to <dn>את</dn> what is false, and they have stumbled from their ways, from the ancient paths, to walk in bypaths and not on a highway,</dq>
[16] <dq>to make their land become a ruin, a hissing forever – everyone who passes by it is appalled and shakes his head.</dq>
[17] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy; <dn>I</dn> shall show them <dn>את</dn> the back and not the face in the day of their calamity.”</dq>

readings.title: A Plot Against the Prophet
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah's Cry for Justice
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 18:18] Then they said, “Come and let us devise plans against Yirmeyahu, for the Torah shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come and let us strike <dn>את</dn> him with the tongue, and let us not listen to any of his words.”
[19] Attend to me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and listen to the voice of my adversaries!
[20] Should good be repaid with evil? For they have dug a pit for <dn>את</dn> my life. Remember that I stood before You to speak good for them, and to turn away Your wrath from them.
[21] So give their children over to scarcity of food, and hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become widows and bereaved of their children. Let their men be killed to death, their young men be stricken by the sword in battle.
[22] Let a cry be heard from their houses, when You bring a raiding party suddenly upon them. For they have dug a pit to take me, and laid snares for my feet.
[23] But You, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, You know <dn>את</dn> all their counsel against me, to slay me. Do not pardon <dn>את</dn> their crookedness, nor blot out <dn>את</dn> their sin from Your presence, and let them be overthrown before You. Deal with them in the time of Your displeasure.

readings.title: The Test of the Rěḵaḇites
readings.subtitle: An Example of Enduring Faithfulness
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 35:1] The word which came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the days of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying,
[2] <dq>“Go to <dn>את</dn> the house of the Rěḵaḇites. And you shall speak to them, and bring <dn>את</dn> them into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.”</dq>
[3] And I took <dn>את</dn> Ya‛azanyah the son of Yirmeyahu, the son of Ḥaḇatstsinyah, and <dn>את</dn> his brothers and <dn>את</dn> all his sons, and <dn>את</dn> all the house of the Rěḵaḇites,
[4] and brought <dn>את</dn> them into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, into the room of the sons of Ḥanan son of Yiḡdalyahu, a man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, which was by the chamber of the heads, above the room of Ma‛asěyahu son of Shallum, the keeper of the door.
[5] And I set before the sons of the house of the Rěḵaḇites bowls filled with wine, and cups, and I said to them, “Drink wine.”
[6] But they said, “We do not drink wine, because Yonaḏaḇ the son of Rěḵaḇ, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘You shall not drink wine, neither you nor your sons, forever.
[7] And do not build a house, neither sow seed, nor plant a vineyard, nor have any of these, but dwell in tents all your days, so that you live many days on the face of the land where you are sojourners.’
[8] “So we obeyed the voice of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rěḵaḇ, our father, in all that he commanded us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
[9] nor to build ourselves houses to dwell in. And we have no vineyard, field or seed.
[10] “But we dwell in tents, and have obeyed and done according to all that Yonaḏaḇ our father commanded us.
[11] “And it came to be, whenNeḇuḵaḏretst-sar sovereign of Baḇel came up into the land, that we said, ‘Come, let us go to Yerushalayim for fear of the army of the Kasdim and for fear of the army of the Arameans.’ So we dwell at Yerushalayim.”

readings.title: A Contrast in Covenants
readings.subtitle: The Rěḵaḇites' Blessing and Judah's Curse
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 35:12] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
[13] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Go, and you shall say to <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, “Have you not received instruction, to obey <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[14] <dq>“<dn>את</dn> The words of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rěḵaḇ, which he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, are established, and they have not drunk unto this day, for they have obeyed their father’s command. And as for <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not obeyed <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[15] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> sent to you <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, saying, ‘Turn, each one from his evil way, and make good your deeds, and do not go after other mighty ones to serve them, and you shall dwell in the land which <dn>I</dn> have given you and your fathers.’ But you have not inclined your ear, nor obeyed <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[16] <dq>“The sons of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rěḵaḇ have indeed carried out <dn>את</dn> the command of their father which he commanded them, but this people has not obeyed <dn>Me</dn>.” ’</dq>
[17] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing on Yehuḏah and on all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim <dn>את</dn> all the evil <dn>I</dn> have pronounced against them, because <dn>I</dn> have spoken to them but they did not listen, and <dn>I</dn> have called to them but they did not answer.’ ”</dq>
[18] And Yirmeyahu said to the house of the Rěḵaḇites, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Because you have obeyed <dn>את</dn> the command of Yonaḏaḇ your father, and guarded <dn>את</dn> all his commands and done according to all that he commanded you,</dq>
[19] <dq>therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “Of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rěḵaḇ there shall never cease to be a man to stand before <dn>Me</dn>.” ’ ”</dq>
